goal_checks.notes: postgres.NewPool sets DefaultQueryExecMode=Exec and StatementCacheCapacity=0 unconditionally, plus sizing from config; matches §7.9's required snippet field-for-field.
jwt.go fetches JWKS, caches by kid, refetches once on unknown kid, validates RS256/ES256 + issuer + required expiry; verified by 4 unit test cases including a real generated RSA keypair.

authorizer.go SQL checked line-by-line against thinkboard-schema-final.sql's current_profile_id()/is_team_member()/is_team_leader()/can_access_session() bodies — same table/column names, same join chain, same role filter.
CachedAuthorizer default TTL wired to config.MembershipCacheTTL (60s); TTL hit/miss and per-key isolation both covered by tests.

middleware.Auth() and RequireTeamMember/RequireSessionAccess implemented as real Gin middleware taking narrow interfaces (testable, no concrete auth.* import needed by the middleware package itself beyond kernel types).

GET /v1/me wired behind Auth(); manual curl confirms 401 paths, and unit tests cover the pieces that would produce a 200 (JWT verify + profile resolution) independently since no live Supabase project/signed JWT was available in this session.

cross_check_against_plan.section: §1 'nothing else may query team_members for authorization'
cross_check_against_plan.result: Only internal/auth/authorizer.go references team_members; grep confirms no other package does.
httpapi -> auth -> {shared/errs, shared/kernel}; auth -> platform not needed (pool passed in from cmd, not imported by auth). No feature package imports platform. Direction preserved.

cross_check_against_plan.section: §7.9 required pgx settings under transaction pooling
cross_check_against_plan.result: Applied unconditionally in postgres.NewPool, matching the doc's snippet exactly (QueryExecModeExec, StatementCacheCapacity=0).
Authorizer SQL is a structural match — same tables, same join path, same role='leader' condition.

issues_found: Real end-to-end verification against a live Supabase project (real signed JWT, real team_members rows) was not possible in this session — recommend running this against `supabase start` with a real user before treating /v1/me or any future route behind Auth()/RequireTeamMember as production-ready.

If the target Supabase project issues HS256 (legacy shared-secret) JWTs rather than using JWKS/asymmetric signing, jwt.go will reject every token as-is — needs an HS256 fallback path if that's the case (see analyze.json open_questions).
